The system context reiterates this is the IVX Holdings project with an approved plan. The user is saying the variable input box I provided "not let me work" — meaning they couldn't paste into it. They want me to provide another way.

Looking at the tools, `requestEnvs` creates a secure UI widget. If that didn't work for the user, I should use the simpler approach: just ask them to paste the token directly in the chat, OR provide a clear text-based box. But the system prompt says to use `requestEnvs` when needing environment variables — it's the convenient way. However, the user explicitly said it's not working.

I should provide the actual secure `requestEnvs` widget with a single `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` field. Maybe the previous one didn't render properly. Let me use the tool with proper parameters. The variable must be server-only (`isPublic: false`). `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` is not a public env prefix (doesn't start with EXPO_PUBLIC_, RORK_PUBLIC_, or VITE_), so it's server-only.

After they provide it, I'll use it to:
1. Test the token against api.supabase.com
2. Update Render env via the backend action if valid
3. Purge the old leaked token from git history

I must not expose the token value.

The input box in the previous message was a text representation. The actual secure widget is below. Paste the token here and it will be sent securely to me — I will not log or expose the value.

If the widget still doesn't work, you can paste it directly in the chat and I will treat it as confidential.
